name: P_LoadLocation
summary: Ends the scheduler's frame: the calling task gets int 1 and continues on the next frame.
semantics: No arguments are read. The handler resumes the task with int 1 (ResumeTaskWithIntVm) and then returns 0 from the dispatcher, which makes the interpreter stop the whole scheduler for this frame (the tasks after the caller in this frame's run are not run until the next frame). The caller's pc and stack top were saved at the call before dispatch; it stays runnable with its result ready and continues with 1 on the next frame. No location is loaded: the name is historical (X2). A savegame taken between the frames stores the task at this call site, so the call behaves like a one-frame yield.
notes: waits=true in the sense of a yield: not state 2, but the step aborts (dispatcher returns 0 -> execution_frame.hpp StopScheduler) and the task resumes from the saved pc next frame. sync_scan's resume test would class it sync.

name: P_Leave
summary: Quits the game process at once with the given exit code (Main::ExitRoutine).
semantics: Calls Main::ExitRoutine((ushort)code) and never returns: the program shuts down (settings written unless suppressed, devices released, process exit). code 0 is the normal quit; a non-zero code shows an error message box with the exit message table text g_ExitMessages[code] (40 entries, 0..0x27) before the exit. The task never gets a result. Used by the main menu's Quit.
x3_src: differs: B16 (fixed) - code 0x28 gets its own title, other out-of-table codes do not index past the table
bugs: AP 0x00497ba8 -> Main::ExitRoutine 0x00401dd0: the script's code indexes the 40-entry message table without a bound (MOVSX ECX,SI at 0x004025da); P_Leave with a code >= 40 shows garbage or faults in the error box. x3_src fixed (bugs_fixed.md B16).

name: P_PrepareInterruption
summary: Pauses every playing movie/music/speech media record and releases the tasks waiting on them.
semantics: Media::StopAllMedia: for every media record flagged playing: pauses it, clears the playing flag, completes the task that waits on it (its MOV_PlayMovie / MOV_PlayMovieFrom / MOV_PlayMovieVoice caller) with int 1 through the owner group's int-completion callback, and clears the record's group/task. Records stay loaded (a later MOV_PlayMovie restarts them). Then the caller gets int 0. Called by scripts before blocking states (save/load, pause).
notes: x3_src also submits the sound frame at once (not visible to scripts).

name: P_SetEngineFlags
summary: No-op stub: answers int 0.
semantics: The case goes to the dispatcher default: the task result is set to int 0 and the task is resumed. Arguments are ignored; nothing is changed.

name: P_ClearEngineFlags
summary: No-op stub: answers int 0.
semantics: Same default case as P_SetEngineFlags: result int 0, nothing changed.

name: P_GetSysFlags
summary: Returns the engine's system flag word (EngineConfig catalogueFlags).
semantics: Answers EngineConfig catalogueFlags. Bit 0x20 is set at startup and cleared by the +r switch; the other bits are startup/launcher state; scripts treat it as an opaque settings word that P_SetSysFlags writes back.
notes: FL Ghidra mislabels the field (halfTangentVertexSize); same slot role by position in the identical dispatcher.

name: P_SetSysFlags
summary: Overwrites the engine's system flag word and returns the new value.
semantics: EngineConfig catalogueFlags = flags (raw dword of arg1, type unchecked); answers the same value. No validation, no side effect beyond the store (readers see it at their next use; the word is saved with the settings at shutdown).

name: P_GetSysD3DFlags
summary: Returns the video/D3D feature flag word (graphics settings).
semantics: Answers EngineConfig video_d3d_flags (x3_src videoFeatureFlags): the graphics options word the settings menu reads and writes (e.g. 0x400 depth clears, 0x800000 automatic view distance / cull LOD, 0x2000000 mipmaps).

name: P_SetSysD3DFlags
summary: Overwrites the video/D3D feature flag word and returns it.
semantics: EngineConfig video_d3d_flags = flags; answers flags. No validation; the renderer reads the bits at their next use.

name: P_GetSysD3DFlags2
summary: Returns the second renderer flag word (graphics settings, part 2).
semantics: Answers EngineConfig rendererFlags (D3D flags 2). Bit 0x8 managed resources; the graphics menu keeps more options in it.
x3_src: differs: same read; the x3_src renderer gives new meanings to bits of this word (0x20000/0x40000 indirect lighting Off/SSAO, 0x80000 RT shadows off, 0x700000 UI scale) - new options, not a bugs.md item

name: P_SetSysD3DFlags2
summary: Overwrites the second renderer flag word and returns it.
semantics: EngineConfig rendererFlags = flags; answers flags. No validation.
x3_src: differs: same store; the x3_src renderer reads new option bits from it (see P_GetSysD3DFlags2)

name: P_GetSysViewDistance
summary: Returns the configured view distance setting.
semantics: Answers EngineConfig videoViewDistance (the graphics menu's view distance; <= 0 means automatic, see P_SetSysViewDistance).
notes: FL Ghidra names the field videoAntialiasMode; same slot by the identical dispatcher position and the 0x800000 coupling.

name: P_SetSysViewDistance
summary: Sets the view distance setting; a value <= 0 also sets the D3D flag 0x800000, > 0 clears it.
semantics: EngineConfig videoViewDistance = distance (signed); if distance < 1 then video_d3d_flags |= 0x800000 else video_d3d_flags &= ~0x800000. Answers distance.

name: P_GetSysShaderQuality
summary: Returns the shader quality setting (read only, there is no setter).
semantics: Answers EngineConfig videoShaderQuality.

name: P_GetSysProfilingFlags
summary: Returns the command-line/launcher flag word (EngineConfig cmdFlags).
semantics: Answers EngineConfig cmdFlags: 0x4 registry settings loaded, 0x8 ignore registry, 0x10 non-interactive (automatic) run, 0x40 do not save settings, 0x200 -profi, 0x400 -generaterdf, 0x800 -convertbodies, 0x1000 -dumpusedbodies.

name: P_SetSysProfilingFlags
summary: Overwrites the command-line/launcher flag word and returns it.
semantics: EngineConfig cmdFlags = flags; answers flags. No validation (e.g. setting 0x40 suppresses the settings save at shutdown).

name: P_ViewEBMFullscreen
summary: Shows a full-screen image and blocks the whole game until the time runs out or a mouse button is pressed.
semantics: Loading::LogoLoop(name, seconds): the image path is 'true/<name>' (or 'h256/<name>' at <= 8 bpp), put through the loading-screen path format and loaded as a texture; not found -> answers 0 at once. Otherwise it is stretched to the back buffer and presented, then the engine busy-waits (frame clock ticks and window messages; no game frames, no scripts) first while a mouse button is still held, then until a fresh left/right button press or until seconds*1000 ms of wall time since showing; the image is freed and the answer is 1. The task does not wait (synchronous), but the whole game is frozen during the call. Used by the intro/exit image sequences.
x3_src: differs: B140 (fixed) - a name >= 232 bytes or a non-string answers 0
bugs: AP Loading::LogoLoop 0x004972d0: the script name is sprintf'ed ('true/%s', then the load-screen format) into two 264-byte stack buffers without a length check: a long name overflows the stack; a non-string arg passes NULL. x3_src fixed (bugs_fixed.md B140).

name: P_ViewLoadingScreen
returns: int 1 drawn (or nothing loadable) / 0 deadline not reached
summary: Draws a loading-screen image with its top/bottom (and gamepad) overlays and presents it, unless the deadline has not come yet.
semantics: Loading::LoadingScreen(name, deadline, force). If force == 0: ticks the frame clock and if wallTime - deadline < 0 (wrapping ms compare) answers 0 without drawing. Otherwise loads name as a texture (a non-string/NULL name or a failed load falls back to 'true/LoadScrDefault'; if that fails too it answers 1 with nothing drawn), loads the overlays 'true/LoadScrTOP', 'true/LoadScrBOT' and, unless a rendererFlags bit disables it, 'true/LoadScrGAMEPAD', draws all layers, ends/presents the frame and frees every texture. Answers 1. Synchronous; the picture stays until the next frame is drawn.
x3_src: differs: B141 (fixed) - a name >= 252 bytes is treated as NULL; suffix checks of a short name no longer read before the string
bugs: AP texture::loadFile 0x004f3510 (reached from here): the script file name is copied/formatted into a 268-byte stack buffer without a length check (stack overflow on a long name); suffix tests read before a short name. x3_src fixed (bugs_fixed.md B141).

name: P_InitLoadingScreen
summary: Rebuilds the list of loading-screen JPEGs and picks a random start image for P_ShowNextLoadingScreen.
semantics: Loading::EnumLoadScreenImages: next-change time = now, index 0, 'initial image' flag set; the catalogue is cleared and refilled with every *.jpg (case-insensitive suffix, name longer than 4 chars) in folder addon/loadscr (FL: addon2/loadscr), numbered 1..n; with 2 or more images the start index is rand()*n/(RAND_MAX+1). Answers 0.
fl: differs: scans addon2/loadscr instead of addon/loadscr

name: P_ShowNextLoadingScreen
summary: Shows the current loading-screen image if its change time has come, then advances to the next one.
semantics: Loading::CycleLoadScreenImage: image = catalogue entry index+1 (index wrapped to 0 if out of range; NULL when the list is empty, which falls back to LoadScrDefault); LoadingScreen(image, nextChange, initialFlag); if it drew (returned 1): nextChange = now + fixed interval, index++ (wrapping to 0), initial flag cleared. Called every frame during loading by the scripts. Answers 0.

name: P_ClearScreen
summary: Clears the display surface (black).
semantics: Render::ClearDisplaySurface, then answers 0.

name: P_GetLocalizedKey
summary: Returns the text that the key at the input queue's read position types in the current keyboard layout, or 0.
semantics: Input::TranslateKeyToText: takes the queued key at the keyboard read index (scan code), maps it through the current keyboard layout (MapVirtualKeyEx + ToUnicodeEx with the current key state, so Shift/AltGr apply) and answers the UTF-8 text as a string. No queued key, scan code 0, or no character (dead/function keys) -> int 0. The engine buffer is replaced at the next call; the script gets its own copy. Used by text-input boxes.

name: P_GetKeyName
summary: Returns the display name of a key binding code (keyboard key, mouse/joystick button or axis) for the controls menu, or 0.
semantics: Input::KeyCodeToName((short)code, alternate). key = code & 0xfff, bit 0x1000 = Shift modifier. Keys outside the special range 0x118..0x147 are keyboard keys: the VK is mapped to a DirectInput scan code (0 -> int 0) and named by the keyboard device's object name; a single upper-case letter without Shift and with alternate == 0 is answered lower-case; with Shift: '<modifier text>+<name>' (modifier text = page 0x76f id 0x24ab8). Special codes 0x118..0x147 (mouse buttons/axes, joystick buttons/axes/hat) are named from text page 0x76f; Shift adds the modifier prefix; bit 0x2000 / 0x4000 prepends text 0x4e3e / 0x4e3f ('%s %s'). Not nameable -> int 0. The string is copied into the script.
x3_src: differs: new - joystick buttons of extra GameInput devices (wide key codes), and the primary's buttons while another device is bound, are named '<device>: Joystick Button #n' (controller work; a feature, not a bugs.md item)
notes: The text ids of each special key inside formatSpecialKeyName are not listed here.

name: P_GetJoySensitivity
summary: Returns the joystick sensitivity setting (percent).
semantics: Answers Input::g_JoySensitivity.

name: P_SetJoySensitivity
summary: Sets the joystick sensitivity setting; no range check.
semantics: Input::g_JoySensitivity = arg1 (raw, unclamped); answers 0. Applied by the joystick axis processing at the next input poll.

name: P_GetJoyDeadzone
summary: Returns the global joystick dead zone (percent).
semantics: Answers Input::g_JoystickDeadZonePercent.

name: P_SetJoyDeadzone
summary: Sets the joystick dead zone of every axis (clamped to 99).
semantics: Input::SetJoystickDeadZonePercent(percent): percent >= 100 becomes 99 (no lower clamp; negatives pass); every per-axis dead zone (the 8 entries P_GetJoyAxisDeadzone reads) and the global value are set to it. Answers 0.

name: P_GetJoyAxisDeadzone
summary: Returns one joystick axis's dead zone; axis codes are 0x100..0x107.
semantics: i = axis - 0x100; if 0 <= i < 8 answers g_JoystickAxisDeadZone[i], else 0.

name: P_SetJoyAxisDeadzone
summary: Sets one joystick axis's dead zone (clamped to 99); axis codes are 0x100..0x107.
semantics: percent > 99 -> 99 (no lower clamp); i = axis - 0x100; if 0 <= i < 8 then g_JoystickAxisDeadZone[i] = percent (only the table entry); other axis values are ignored. Answers 0.

name: P_GetSysIORequirements
summary: Returns the input settings flag word (inverted axes etc.).
semantics: Answers EngineConfig inputFlags. Known bits: 0x80 invert joystick pitch, 0x20 invert joystick yaw, 0x800000 invert mouse pitch, 0x200000 set at startup; other bits are input options stored by the menu.

name: P_SetSysIORequirements
summary: Stores the input settings flag word and applies its invert bits to the live input block.
semantics: EngineConfig inputFlags = flags; then copies bits 0x80 (invert joystick pitch), 0x20 (invert joystick yaw) and 0x800000 (invert mouse pitch) into Input::g_pInputBlock->flags (each set or cleared to match). Answers 0 (not the value, unlike the other P_Set*).
